evidence: Ter. Ad. 729: Et dūcenda indōtāta est?
Plaut. Aul. 480: ut indōtātās dūcant uxōrēs domum
terms.comment: Its opposite is dōtātus, with a dowry, and so with a large one: uxor dōtāta is the rich wife who rules her husband.

phrases.latin: nam quae indōtāta est, ea in potestāte est virī
phrases.english: for a wife without a dowry is in her husband’s power

phrases.latin: Virgō nihil habet. — Audīvī. — Et dūcenda indōtāta est?
phrases.english: The girl has nothing. — So I have heard. — And she is to be married without a dowry?

sources: Lewis & Short: indotatus · Lewis & Short: doto
